scope: Curated reference of 12 verified major operational seaports and maritime export terminals in Nigeria: all 7 major public commercial seaport complexes listed by the Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA) across Western and Eastern Ports (including Nigeria's first operational deep-sea port at Lekki) plus 5 major onshore/coastal crude oil, gas-to-liquids, and LNG marine export terminals carrying official UNECE Function-1 seaport UN/LOCODEs within NPA pilotage districts. Explicitly excludes unbuilt greenfield port proposals, minor fishing jetties, private tank-farm piers without public port status, live AIS vessel positions, freight rate quotes, and cargo booking.
prefixChoice: Uses `/ports` rather than `/seaports` so the URL prefix stays short, matches `/airports` and `/airlines`, and naturally accommodates river-estuary ocean ports (Warri, Port Harcourt, Onne, Calabar) alongside coastal deep-sea and hydrocarbon export terminals while keeping page titles and headings anchored on Nigerian seaports.
notes: Under the Nigerian Ports Authority Act (formerly Ports Act 1954) and the 2006 federal port concessioning reform, NPA operates a landlord model across Nigeria's public commercial seaport complexes: the Federal Government retains ownership of port land, quays, breakwaters, and common-user channels while NPA provides marine, pilotage, towage, and ISPS security oversight and private concessionaires operate cargo terminals. UN/LOCODEs follow the United Nations Economic Commission for Europe (UNECE) registry for Nigeria (`NG`), shown in standard 5-character shipping format (`NGXXX`, equivalent to UNECE `NG XXX`).

Situated in Apapa LGA, Lagos State, the complex features road, inland-waterway barge, and standard-gauge/narrow-gauge rail links into Lagos and the hinterland. Since the 2006 federal port reform, the Nigerian Ports Authority serves as statutory landlord and marine regulator while five concessioned terminal operators manage container, dry-bulk, and general-cargo berths alongside port-side flour, sugar, and salt processing plants, eight petroleum/specialty jetties, and offshore logistics bases including LADOL and Eko Support Services.

ports.operationsSummary: Located inside the Lagos Free Zone in Ibeju-Lekki LGA roughly 65 kilometres east of central Lagos, Lekki Deep Sea Port is Nigeria's first operational deep-sea port. Developed under a 45-year Build, Own, Operate, and Transfer (BOOT) public-private partnership among private sponsors China Harbour Engineering Company and Tolaram Group (75%), the Lagos State Government (20%), and the Nigerian Ports Authority (5%), it commenced commercial operations in April 2023. With a 16.5-metre dredged depth and Ship-to-Shore Super Post-Panamax cranes, it handles large container mainline vessels and West African transshipment traffic that cannot enter shallower river or lagoon ports.
keyFacilities: 16.5-metre navigation channel and turning basin engineered for large mainline container vessels (14,000+ TEU class)

Direct integration with the Lagos Free Zone industrial cluster in Ibeju-Lekki and barge connections back to Lagos Lagoon terminals
Statutory marine pilotage and towage services provided by the Nigerian Ports Authority

ports.establishedNote: Crude export operations commenced late 1960s under Gulf Oil (now Chevron); Escravos Gas Plant & EGTL commissioned subsequently
ports.operationsSummary: Situated at the Atlantic mouth of the Escravos River in Warri South West LGA, Delta State, Escravos Marine Terminal (`NGESC`) is the flagship operational complex of the NNPC Limited (60%) and Chevron Nigeria Limited (40%) joint venture. Within the Nigerian Ports Authority's Warri/Delta pilotage corridor, Escravos integrates onshore crude oil storage and offshore Single Point Mooring tanker loading for Escravos Light crude with the Escravos Gas Plant (EGP), the Escravos Gas-to-Liquids (EGTL) synthetic fuels export plant, and onshore compression feeding both the domestic Escravos–Lagos Pipeline System and the West African Gas Pipeline.
keyFacilities: Onshore Escravos crude oil storage complex and subsea pipelines serving offshore Single Point Mooring (SPM) export buoys
Escravos Gas-to-Liquids (EGTL) facility and Escravos Gas Plant (EGP) supporting marine export of synthetic diesel, naphtha, and LPG/condensate
Logistics marine dock and airstrip supporting western Niger Delta swamp and shallow-water operations

ports.name: Brass Marine Oil Terminal
ports.locality: Twon-Brass / Brass Island, Brass River Mouth
ports.landlordAuthority: Nigerian Ports Authority (Eastern Ports Pilotage Zone) with NUPRC & NMDPRA oversight
ports.operator: Oando Energy Resources (formerly Nigerian Agip Oil Company — 40% JV operator) in joint venture with NNPC Limited (60%)
terminalOperators: Oando Energy Resources Nigeria Ltd (acquired NAOC from Eni in August 2024) — Onshore Brass crude oil tank farm & offshore Single Buoy Mooring export loading
ports.role: Central Niger Delta Brass River crude oil storage & offshore export terminal
ports.waterway: Mouth of the Brass River, Central Niger Delta Atlantic Coast
ports.establishedNote: Commissioned 1973 by Nigerian Agip Oil Company (NAOC); operatorship acquired by Oando Plc on 22 August 2024
ports.operationsSummary: Located at Twon-Brass on Brass Island at the mouth of the Brass River in Bayelsa State, the Brass Marine Oil Terminal (`NGBRA`) is the principal maritime export terminal in Bayelsa State, evacuating light sweet Brass River crude gathered from onshore and swamp blocks OMLs 60, 61, 62, and 63 across Bayelsa, Rivers, Delta, and Imo States. Originally developed by Eni's onshore subsidiary Nigerian Agip Oil Company (NAOC) and carrying official UNECE seaport code `NGBRA`, the terminal came under indigenous operatorship on 22 August 2024 when Oando Plc completed its acquisition of NAOC alongside majority JV partner NNPC Limited.
keyFacilities: Onshore crude oil stabilization and storage tank farm on Brass Island, Brass LGA, Bayelsa State
Subsea pipelines feeding offshore Single Buoy Mooring (SBM) export loading points in the Gulf of Guinea
Coastal marine logistics jetty supporting central Niger Delta swamp and island operations
